model: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: Manager's fees paid and payable in units, FY25/26 AR Distribution Statement Note A (S$55.340m; cash flow add-back S$55.731m). Treated as the REIT analogue of SBC: a real operating cost settled in new units.
inputs.share_count_basis: Total issued units 5,110.907m at 31 Mar 2026 (FY25/26 AR Financial Review). Held flat: unit-settled manager's fees (~0.9%/yr of new units) are charged in the flow via sbc_pct_path, so diluting the count as well would double-count. No buybacks; no DRP units issued in FY25/26.
inputs.wacc_rationale: The rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is post-interest. SGD basis: SGS 10y ~2.3% (assumed; not re-fetched for this build) + beta ~0.95 (40.6% aggregate leverage, 30%+ of AUM in China/HK, ~70% non-SGD income only 75% hedged) x 5.5% ERP = ~7.5% base. Bull 7.0%, bear 8.25%. Cross-check: the market prices the unit at a 6.7% trailing headline DPU yield.
inputs.lease_treatment: Ground-lease payments (S$11.5m FY26) are already deducted in amount distributable; no separate lease charge (lease_cost_pct_path 0) to avoid charging twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Amount distributable to Unitholders of MLT is already after NCI distributions (S$1.5m) and after perpetual securities holders (S$22.6m distribution on S$582.4m perps). Perps are thus treated as debt-like via their coupon; net debt held at zero.
inputs.notes: MODEL: REIT AFFO capitalisation at cost of equity, run through the component engine with net debt = 0 (dcf-methods routing: REIT / property trust with IAS 40 fair value and an external manager). Reported net income and FCF are dominated by revaluations, FX translation and acquisition capex and are not used. ENGINE MAPPING: 'revenue' = gross revenue; 'EBITDA margin' = amount distributable to Unitholders (before deducting unit-settled manager's fees) / gross revenue = 370.067/708.274 = 52.25% in FY26 -- i.e. it is already after property expenses, cash manager fees, borrowing costs, tax, lease payments, NCI and perpetual distributions, so interest-rate and refinancing risk live in the margin path; D&A 0 and cash tax 0 because both are inside distributable income. 'SBC' = manager's fees paid in units (7.81% of revenue). 'Capex' = maintenance/sustaining capex not funded in distributable income, assumed 4.0% of revenue base (~S$28m; FY26 additions to investment properties were S$120.6m but include the Joo Koon redevelopment tail and AEIs; no maintenance split is disclosed -- this is a judgment). House AFFO FY26 = 370.1 - 55.3 - 28.3 = S$286.4m = 5.60c/unit vs 7.262c headline DPU. Street basis adds back the unit-settled fee. DPU base: FY25/26 contains NO divestment-gain distributions (policy discontinued), so 7.262c is a clean run-rate starting point; FY24/25's 8.053c included S$27.0m of gains (adjusted 7.519c). VINTAGE: balance sheet and unit count are the 31 Mar 2026 annual; the 1Q FY26/27 business update (late Jul 2026) and 1H FY26/27 results (late Oct 2026) are not in the folder -- refresh the guidance year when they are extracted.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: per-unit DPU has compounded at ~0% over FY14-FY26 (7.35c -> 7.262c) while equity 5yr CAGR (2.64%) reflects unit issuance for acquisitions, not per-unit growth; 1.5% is the base terminal per-unit growth
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGR (-24% 3yr, -15% 5yr) diverges by far more than 30% from equity and revenue CAGRs because REIT EPS is dominated by fair-value and FX translation movements; EPS is meaningless for this model. FCF CAGRs here are per-unit DPU CAGRs (FY23 9.011c, FY21 8.326c -> FY26 7.262c), the cleanest owner-flow series available; 3yr is depressed by the end of divestment-gain distributions.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue 5yr CAGR is acquisition-driven (AUM S$10.8bn FY21 -> S$13.1bn FY26) and funded with new units and debt (gearing 38.4% -> 40.6%), so it did not reach unitholders per unit.

base.terminal_cap_multiple_note: set just above the Gordon-implied 16.9x so the perpetuity at CoE governs
base.narrative: FY27 revenue -1.5%: full-year loss of the six FY26 divestments (~S$99m), continued SGD strength against regional currencies, China reversions still negative; offset by Joo Koon and Mumbai contributions and +4% ex-China reversions. Margin dips ~0.6pt in FY27-28 as hedges roll and refinanced debt reprices above the 2.6% average cost, then recovers slowly as divestment proceeds pay down debt. Per-unit growth settles at 2.0% (rent escalators in developed markets) and fades to 1.5% terminal, consistent with a trust that has delivered ~0% DPU growth over twelve years.

bull.narrative: China reversions turn positive by FY28, the ~S$1bn divestment programme recycles low-yield China/HK assets into higher-growth India/Vietnam/Australia sponsor-pipeline assets accretively, regional rates fall so refinancing is neutral, and the SGD stops appreciating. Per-unit growth 3% mid-decade, 2.0% terminal; cost of equity compresses toward 7.0% as gearing falls below 38%.

bear.narrative: China and Hong Kong oversupply persists (national China vacancy ~20%, HK prime warehouse 10%), divestments are dilutive, SGD keeps strengthening, and the 17% floating plus rolling hedges reprice 75-100bp higher (management's own sensitivity: +100bp cuts ICR from 2.9x to 2.2x). Margin falls ~2.7pt; per-unit growth 1%; cost of equity 8.25% as gearing presses toward 42-43%. Not a solvency case: BBB+, S$716m committed undrawn facilities, only S$89m maturing in FY27.

scenario_narratives.base: Operational DPU has been steady for four quarters at ~1.81-1.82c; FY27 drifts lower on divestments and FX, then low-single-digit rent escalation resumes. House AFFO deducts the ~S$55m of manager's fees paid in units and ~S$28m of sustaining capex, so the house yield on price is materially below the headline 6.7% DPU yield.
scenario_narratives.bull: Portfolio rejuvenation works: China trough passes, capital recycled into sponsor pipeline in India/Vietnam/Australia, refinancing neutral, SGD stable; per-unit growth ~3% and cost of equity 7.0%.
scenario_narratives.bear: China/HK weakness and SGD strength persist, refinancing costs rise, gearing creeps up; margin compresses ~2.7pt and per-unit growth is ~1%, valued at an 8.25% cost of equity.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than the house 15/50/35: DPU has fallen four years running, ~40% of AUM sits in the two weakest markets (China, HK), gearing is at a cycle high and ~70% of income is non-SGD. Bear is not a solvency case (BBB+, ample committed facilities), so it is not weighted above 25%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value what unitholders actually receive per unit, not what the trust reports. Distributable income is the right starting flow for an S-REIT, but it adds back the manager's fees paid in new units -- a real cost to existing holders -- and it does not fund sustaining capex. The house basis deducts both and capitalises the remainder at an SGD cost of equity with net debt at zero (the flow is already after interest and perpetual coupons). The street basis treats unit-settled fees as non-cash, as most broker DDMs do. NAV (S$1.26/unit, Mar 2026) is a cross-check, not the valuation: it carries the valuers' cap rates and FX marks.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: each 50bp moves base value by roughly 8-9% (capitalised flow with low growth)
Refinancing: 2.6% average cost of debt is below current regional rates; hedge roll-off feeds straight into the margin path
China/HK: 40.6% of AUM; continued negative reversions or dilutive divestments
FX: ~70% non-SGD income, 75% hedged 12 months forward; S$325m translation loss on valuations in FY26
Sustaining-capex assumption (4% of revenue) is a judgment; no maintenance split is disclosed
Sponsor conflicts: ROFR acquisition pricing and fee structure (base and performance fees partly in units)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 1.06-1.37 SGD
data_sources.financials: FY25/26 Annual Report (Distribution Statements p.122, Note A; Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows p.123-124; Financial Review p.37); M44U.SI_Metrics.csv (core_metrics) and kpis table for DPU, NAV, gearing, ICR, WALE, occupancy history
